chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام): “By what do you judge when you judge?”
He said: “By the judgment of Allah and the judgment of Dawud. So when a matter comes to us that is not with us, Ruh al-Qudus conveys it to us.”

key_terms.الشَّيْءَ: the matter or thing brought for judgment
key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah; the divine source of judgment
key_terms.بِحُكْمِ: by the judgment; the basis of authoritative ruling
key_terms.دَاوُدَ: Dawud; the prophet whose mode of judgment is referenced
key_terms.رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ: the Holy Spirit; the means by which the matter is conveyed to them

ai.seo_question: By what does Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) judge, and how does he receive knowledge of new matters?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Imam Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) judges by the judgment of Allah and the judgment of Dawud. It also indicates that when a matter comes to the Imam for which no prior ruling is presently with them, Ruh al-Qudus conveys it to them, highlighting divinely assisted knowledge and authority.
